cues: Two defects follow straight from geometry.
In myopia, short sight, the eyeball is too long, so distant objects focus in front of the retina; a concave, diverging lens fixes it.
In hypermetropia, long sight, the eyeball is too short and the image would fall behind the retina; a convex, converging lens fixes it.
